exercise.name: Band Incline Row

reference.title: Band Incline Row
reference.listing: Video (movement reference only; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment, so the data sheet was not read; the set-up, chest on an incline bench with the band anchored low in front, follows the name and the dumbbell version)

exercise.mechanics: Compound (shoulder extension, scapular retraction, elbow flexion)

breathing.pattern: Exhale as you row, inhale as you lower; let the chest stay on the pad.
breathing.cadence: About 1.1 s up, 0.4 s squeeze, 2 s down

prescription.load: Band tension is user-chosen; stop about 1-3 reps short of failure (RIR 1-3)
prescription.progression: More reps, a stronger band, or the rack further away; pause at the top

cues.text: Bench at about 40 degrees, band looped low round a rack upright in front. Straddle the seat, chest on the pad with the chin just over the top, feet planted behind; a strand in each hand, arms hanging straight.
Breathe out and drive the elbows up and back toward the hips, close to the body.
Squeeze the shoulder blades back; the hands reach the sides of the lower ribs and the band is at its tightest.
Breathe in and lower under control until the arms are straight; do not let the band pull them down.
Let the shoulder blades glide forward a little, keep the back flat, repeat.

mistakes.mistake: Lifting the chest off the pad to heave the band
mistakes.fix: Keep the chest on the pad; use a lighter band.
Keep the head in line with the trunk, eyes down and forward.
Pull the elbows back toward the hips.

mistakes.mistake: Letting the band snap the arms down

kinematics.norm: From nearly straight to about 90 degrees (clinical opinion)
The chest stays on the pad through the rep (clinical opinion)

Anchored low in front, the band pulls the hands down and forward; its tension rises as it stretches, so the load is highest at the top of the row (at matched effort elastic tubing and dumbbells gave similar muscle activity; Andersen 2010)
Controlled, about 1 s up and 2 s down (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #16970, Band Incline Row, video (movement reference)
Fenwick, Brown & McGill 2009, comparison of different rowing exercises: trunk muscle activation and lumbar spine motion, load and stiffness (J Strength Cond Res 23(2):350-358)
Lehman et al. 2004, variations in muscle activation levels during traditional latissimus dorsi weight training exercises (Dynamic Medicine 3:4)

Andersen, Andersen, Mortensen, Poulsen, Bjornlund and Zebis 2010, muscle activation and perceived loading during rehabilitation exercises: comparison of dumbbells and elastic resistance (Phys Ther 90(4):538-549)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness, tingling or giving-way occurs.
Check the band for nicks or tears and loop it securely round the upright, low down, so it cannot slide up.
Band tension is your choice: pick one you can row to the ribs with the form shown for every rep.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Check the bench pin is locked at the chosen angle before lying on it.
modify: Low-back pain: this supported row is usually a good choice because the pad holds the trunk (clinical opinion).
Shoulder pain: shorten the top of the range.

muscleNotes.lats_r: Extend the shoulders, pulling the elbows back beside the trunk.
muscleNotes.lats_l: Extend the shoulders, pulling the elbows back beside the trunk.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Retract the shoulder blades; rows give the highest middle trapezius/rhomboid activity of common pulls (Lehman 2004).
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Retract the shoulder blades; rows give the highest middle trapezius/rhomboid activity of common pulls (Lehman 2004).
muscleNotes.core: Light bracing only: the pad holds the trunk, so the low back does not have to hold a hinge (clinical opinion; compare the high lumbar demand of the free-standing bent-over row in Fenwick 2009).

phases.label: Chest on the pad, arms hanging
